facts.text: Pentonville lies in northern Clerkenwell, while the south is often called Farringdon after the railway station that itself took its name from Farringdon Road.
In the 1920s and 1930s, 37a Clerkenwell Green hosted Communist Party meetings, later becoming the site of the Marx Memorial Library founded in 1933.
The well that gave Clerkenwell its name was rediscovered in 1924, revealing the area's ancient water source.
Near Clerkenwell's boundary with the City of London, the Charterhouse began as a Carthusian monastery before becoming a historic school.
Kodak United opened a factory at 41–43 Clerkenwell, exploiting local jewelers and watchmakers to build and repair stereoscopic cameras.
Clerkenwell Green has had no grass for over 300 years, preserving its historic village‑centre feel.
